AssertionStatus.description: The authority model on an assertion, from fss-policy-kg's overlay discipline.
AssertionStatus.title: AssertionStatus

Citation.description: Any citation appearing in a governed document, captured at ingest in state `proposed` (AD-030-R6). Verification is a transition carrying method, date and by.

asserted_at.description: When the assertion was made, ISO 8601 UTC.

doc_id.description: The Document a child node belongs to.

id.description: The readable, source-scoped key the graph minted at admission. It never changes and is never reused; a name is a property (DI-060, DI-062, OD-4 §3.1).

method.description: How the assertion was made (manifest, crossref, openalex, github, human_ruling, ...).

prov_wasDerivedFrom.description: The manifest entry or source the assertion was derived from.

prov_wasGeneratedBy.description: Run id of the activity that made the assertion.

raw.description: The citation exactly as the document writes it.

ruling_id.description: The event id of the human ruling that authorized this assertion, when one did.

superseded_by.description: The event id of the assertion that replaced this one. Never a deletion (DI-053, DI-064).

text.description: The verbatim span. Never paraphrased; the hash is over the file, not over this.

CitationState.description: AD-030-R6. Capture is free; verification is a separate, recorded transition.

CitoType.description: CiTO (Shotton 2010), the subset AD-030-R7 names. `disagrees_with` and `refutes` carry a `reason` naming the constraint that no longer holds: rejected science stays in the graph as a rejected prescription rather than vanishing from it.

DocKind.description: Which governed directory the document came from. The directory is the document's genre and decides how hard its citation gate is (AD-030-R6: a design note ships with `proposed` citations, a paper does not).
DocKind.title: DocKind

Document.description: One governed markdown file. `id` is its repo-relative path slugged; `path` is the live edit surface; `content_hash` is what identity actually rests on (AD-030-R4).

asserted_at.description: When the assertion was made, ISO 8601 UTC.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the file as it stood when the assertion was made (AD-030-R4).

id.description: The readable, source-scoped key the graph minted at admission. It never changes and is never reused; a name is a property (DI-060, DI-062, OD-4 §3.1).

identifiers.description: Every identifier reference the node's text names (`AD-030`, `DN-4`, an eight-hex task id prefix), recovered lexically. Squiddy turns the ones that resolve inside THIS graph into `Mentions` edges; the rest are carried here because they resolve in Seldon's graph, not in this one, and `seldon governed sync` is what can see them (AD-030-R10: the coupling is a stream, not awareness). A reference that is dropped rather than carried is a link the graph can never recover.

ManifestDisposition.description: Axis 2, intent or role, profiling DDI-Lifecycle 3.3 with local reason codes. A graph's config restricts this to the values it uses; a value not in the config is a gate failure.
ManifestDisposition.title: ManifestDisposition

ManifestEntry.description: One entry per document ever considered (DI-070). The two status axes are required.

cited_in.description: Where in the graph's own record this item is cited; the biblio assessment criterion.

id.description: The readable, source-scoped key the graph minted at admission. It never changes and is never reused; a name is a property (DI-060, DI-062, OD-4 §3.1).

ManifestStage.description: Axis 1, pipeline position, profiling UNECE GSBPM v5.1 (icsp_notebook/corpus/manifest_schema.md). `admitting` is `in_graph` in the middle of becoming true (v7.11, DI-078).
ManifestStage.title: ManifestStage

ManifestState.description: AD-030-R5. Every document ever considered is a node from the moment it is cataloged. A `declined` node carries its reason and never receives a content edge; reopening one requires a new decision with a `supersedes` edge.
ManifestState.title: ManifestState

Mentions.description: (any)-[:MENTIONS]->(any), recovered lexically from an identifier reference: `AD-NNN`, `DN-`, `S-NNN`, `TN-N`, or an eight-hex task id prefix. The weakest edge in the set, and the one that finds the most.
